text:
sam (support): heads-up: ACME reported streaming sessions dropping on their dedicated VPC deployment. They see partial output then an immediate reset from a corporate proxy. Happening on their on-prem ingress -> our private pool. They filed traces and a short curl repro.

maria (sre): thanks. can you paste the curl repro + the tcpdump snippet? also which model/route are they hitting?

sam (support): reproducer they provided (simplified):
```bash
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \ 
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \ 
  'https://private.redwood.example/api/v1/streams?model=redwood-mini'
```
Their client shows: first few event chunks, then connection RST from the corporate proxy. tcpdump on their ingress shows MSS/MTU mismatches: I can paste excerpt.

maria (sre): paste the tcpdump excerpt please. my suspicion: PMTU/MTU blackhole combined with a proxy terminating long-lived SSE connections and doing aggressive idle-timeout or rewriting chunking.

sam (support): tcpdump log (simplified):
```
15:02:01.123 IP 10.0.0.5.52344 > 10.1.1.9.443: Flags [P.], seq 1201:1980, ack 502, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123 ecr 456], length 779
15:02:02.002 IP 10.1.1.9.443 > 10.0.0.5.52344: Flags [P.], seq 502:1181, ack 1980, win 65535, options [mss 1400], length 679
15:02:02.300 IP 10.0.0.5.52344 > 10.1.1.9.443: Flags [R], seq 1980, win 0, length 0
```
we see the server -> client chunk larger than observed MSS and then an R. ACME says this only manifests through their corporate proxy (they tested direct to on-prem ingress and it works).

maria (sre): interesting. if direct to ingress works then the proxy likely rewrites or buffers. do we have the proxy product (vendor) name?

sam (support): they said "CorpProxy v4.2" (internal appliance). They also said the proxy strips Transfer-Encoding: chunked and forces Content-Length for some responses, but for SSE chunk boundaries that's destructive.

kate (eng-runtime): jumping in. Two hypotheses: 1) PMTU blackhole where a middlebox drops ICMP 'need fragment' and later resets long-lived connection after a large chunk. 2) Proxy rewriting chunking and then hitting connection size guard/keepalive which triggers RST. Both can cause partial output.

sam (support): ACME also observed intermittent "502 Bad Gateway" from the proxy just before RST. I've attached the proxy logs they pasted: 
```
[2026-03-01T15:02:02Z] ERROR upstream: recv() failed: connection reset by peer
[2026-03-01T15:02:02Z] WARN rewriting transfer-encoding: chunked -> content-length
```

maria (sre): ok. immediate triage steps I recommended to customer: 1) try `curl --http1.1 -N` to avoid HTTP/2 multiplexing differences. 2) set SSE keepalive/ping interval to 10s on client side and add `X-Accel-Buffering: no` or `Cache-Control: no-transform` on the response to discourage proxy buffering. 3) confirm MTU on their egress path (10.0.0.5 saw mtu 1500 but proxy advertised 1400).

sam (support): ACME ran step 1 and sent results: switching to HTTP/1.1 reduced occurrences but didn't eliminate them. They added a 10s heartbeat and # of disconnects dropped by ~70%. They can't change the proxy config widely (security constraints).

kate (eng-runtime): good signal. two immediate product-side mitigations we can propose: - make server chunk sizes <= 1200 bytes for SSE events (avoid hitting lowered MSS). We can add an SSE chunk-splitter in the private runtime config as a short term. - enable periodic tiny keepalive bytes (single "\n" events) every 8s to keep proxy from idling.

maria (sre): is chunk-splitting doable via route-level config or do we need an eng deploy?

kate (eng-runtime): we can toggle a runtime flag per-tenant: `sse.chunk_max_bytes=1100` and `sse.heartbeat_interval=8s`. It won't require model rebuild. But we need approval from product/security for per-customer config in Private. Also need testing for throughput/cost impact.

sam (support): customer asked about why this is Dedicated/Private-specific — they said Hosted didn't hit this because hosted fronting edge used larger MSS and didn't rewrite chunked encoding. They want a permanent fix.

kate (eng-runtime): that's expected — corporate proxies in on-prem paths vary a lot. For a permanent fix we should: 1) add negotiated SSE chunking to the runtime that adapts to observed peer MSS, 2) expose route config for heartbeat and chunk size, and 3) add a telemetry flag that logs chunk splits and proxy buffer hits for easier debugging.

maria (sre): for tonight can we ship the per-tenant toggles as a config? Or do we need a quick patch?

kate (eng-runtime): I can push a runtime hotfix to enable static chunk-splitting per private deployment (no code changes to model runtime, just middleware). But we need an on-call approval. @ingress-bot can you open a canary and show the config diff?

ingress-bot: created canary deployment 'sse-chunk-splitter-canary' in private-pool-acme with flags: `sse.chunk_max_bytes=1100, sse.heartbeat_interval=8s`. Canary URL: https://canary.private.redwood/acme-sse-check

sam (support): forwarded canary to ACME. they ran quick smoke and reported much better stability for 30 minutes. will monitor longer.

maria (sre): next action items listed: 1) sam to collect 24h of canary telemetry from ACME and proxy logs. 2) kate to draft runtime PR for adaptive chunking + config UI. 3) support reply to ACME with workaround and ETA for permanent fix. 4) ops to consider documentation on "on-prem proxy gotchas".

kate (eng-runtime): I'll start the PR and include tests for: - no change in hosted paths, - minimal perf impact for small-event workloads, - logging when we split an event.

sam (support): ACME understands workaround but wants SLA note. I've offered an interim doc we can share.

maria (sre): thanks team. if disconnects spike again ping @kate and I'll open an incident. :thumbsup:

sam (support): closing loop here — will update thread with final logs after 24h. thanks! :white_check_mark:
